# Porchlamp (https://porchlamp.org/)

> A porch lamp left on tells a visitor they are expected. Porchlamp ranks 11,000 open-source projects by what happens to a stranger's pull request, not by how many stars the project has. Every score traces back to recorded GitHub responses and SHA-256 content hashes (by Rahul Kumar, `pctablet505`).

## Findings (snapshot `2026-10-23`)
- **More than 1 in 5.** In Porchlamp's 2026-10-23 snapshot, 844 of 4,125 active open-source projects (20.5%) left most outside pull requests with no human reply, review or merge within 14 days.
- **More stars, more silence.** The share rises with stars: 17% of projects with 1,000 to 10,000 stars, 24% at 10,000 to 50,000, and 27% at 50,000 or more.
- **Fame is no guarantee.** 14 of the 100 most-starred projects are black holes, and only 6 of them reach Porchlamp's top 100.
- **Stars barely predict an answer.** Across 3,991 ranked projects, the rank correlation between stars and the Porchlamp score is 0.11.
- **Most of those pull requests waited.** Inside the black-hole projects, 57,316 of 75,791 counted outside pull requests got no human reply within 14 days.
- We followed 1,443,194 pull requests from 227,261 outside contributors to 11,000 GitHub projects, from 25 April to 22 October 2026.
- 3,991 projects are ranked under the balanced lens; 5,505 are gated and 1,504 unrated, each listed with its reason under [Not ranked](https://porchlamp.org/not-ranked/).

## Static pages (readable without JavaScript)
- [Stars don't review pull requests: the state of open-source black holes (latest snapshot)](https://porchlamp.org/black-holes/)
- [The same report, frozen for citation (snapshot `2026-10-23`)](https://porchlamp.org/black-holes/2026-10-23/)
- [CSV of the 3,991 ranked projects (CC BY 4.0)](https://porchlamp.org/black-holes/2026-10-23/porchlamp-2026-10-23-ranked.csv)
- [Methodology: every gate, pillar, lens, weight and parameter](https://porchlamp.org/methodology/)

## One page per ranked project (readable without JavaScript)
To check a project, open https://porchlamp.org/projects/<owner>/<name>/ (lower case).
Each page opens with the project's median time to a first human reply to an outside pull request, the share that got no reply within 14 days, and its rank overall and for first-time contributors. Example: [meshery/meshery](https://porchlamp.org/projects/meshery/meshery/)

## Ecosystem and lens pages (readable without JavaScript)
Each page lists the top 50 projects of its cut, with score and tier, and each name opens that project's page.
- [Rust projects that answer outside pull requests](https://porchlamp.org/rust/)
- [Python projects that answer outside pull requests](https://porchlamp.org/python/)
- [JavaScript projects that answer outside pull requests](https://porchlamp.org/javascript/)
- [Go projects that answer outside pull requests](https://porchlamp.org/go/)
- [Java projects that answer outside pull requests](https://porchlamp.org/java/)
- [C and C++ projects that answer outside pull requests](https://porchlamp.org/c-cpp/)
- [Open-source projects for first-time contributors](https://porchlamp.org/first-timers/)
- [Open-source projects for building career capital](https://porchlamp.org/career/)
- [Open-source projects for senior systems engineers](https://porchlamp.org/senior-systems/)
- [Open-source projects for AI-assisted contributors](https://porchlamp.org/ai-assisted/)

## 5 pillars and 18 parameters (balanced weights)
1. **Responsiveness (25%):** Time to First Response, Decision Rate (90d), First-timer Merge Rate, PR Ghost Rate (14d), Time to Merge (p90).
2. **Criticality (25%):** Dependents, OpenSSF Criticality, Monthly Downloads.
3. **Governance (20%):** Legal IP Regime, Elephant Factor, Promotion Ladder.
4. **Rigor (15%):** Pipeline Defenses, AI Policy Posture, Substantive Review Rate.
5. **Accessibility (15%):** Newcomer Issue Supply, Newcomer Conversion, Newcomer Return Rate, Developer Experience.
